facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
no breast symptoms
a new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast
no discrete abnormality corresponding to the mammographic finding
a tomosynthesis-guided vacuum-assisted biopsy of the right inner breast was performed
yielding 12 core specimens
marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils
with lymphocytes and plasma cells and no granulomata
no history of urticaria, asthma, angioedema, or pruritus except for seasonal allergic rhinitis
Peripheral blood eosinophil levels were within the normal range
Hypereosinophilic syndrome was excluded from consideration
asymptomatic

concepts.why: The patient has a marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils, with lymphocytes and plasma cells, which is consistent with eosinophilic mastitis.
The patient has a new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast, which could be consistent with fibrocystic change.
The patient has a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis, which is consistent with allergic rhinitis.

The patient has a marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate, which could be consistent with idiopathic granulomatous mastitis, although the absence of granulomata makes this diagnosis less likely.

rationales.F03: Developing asymmetry in the breast is a common finding in various breast conditions.
rationales.F07: Eosinophilic infiltration is a key feature of eosinophilic mastitis.
rationales.F08: The presence of lymphocytes and plasma cells, along with eosinophils, supports an inflammatory process.
rationales.F10: Normal peripheral blood eosinophil levels decrease the likelihood of hypereosinophilic syndrome but do not rule out eosinophilic mastitis.
rationales.F11: The exclusion of hypereosinophilic syndrome focuses the differential diagnosis on other conditions with eosinophilic infiltration.

frontier_selector.rationale: The histologic examination revealed a marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils, which is a key finding that supports Eosinophilic mastitis.
